title: Paper bridge
sampleTitle: Making the handoff between tasks clear
description: A cut-paper bridge joins two separate paper stacks, with a lime coupling marking where one task hands work to the next. An illustrative metaphor for making task handoffs clear.
composition: Oblique close crop of two paper stacks and one connecting bridge on light ivory.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: editorial concept artwork.
Subject: a physically constructed paper sculpture: two simple stacks of matte ivory paper separated by a gap, connected by one elegant simple bridge of cut and folded matte blue and ivory paper strips. A small luminous lime joining piece visibly couples the bridge at its center. The construction should look physically plausible and carefully handmade, with paper thickness, crisp cut edges, slight natural paper variation, and crease folds.
Scene/backdrop: a light warm ivory seamless tabletop and background, predominantly pale and open, not a gradient.
Composition: oblique close crop; the left stack sits closer to camera, the right stack recedes, and the bridge makes a confident diagonal across the gap. Both ends clearly rest on the stacks. The paper sculpture occupies most of the frame while leaving calm ivory space around it. No other props.
Lighting/materials: soft directional daylight with tactile shallow shadows that reveal the edges and folds. Real matte colored paper, not glossy plastic or a digital icon render. Restrained editorial still-life photography.
Palette: ivory #F8FAF5 dominant, matte blue #007EBD on the connecting strips, one small luminous lime #D6FF62 connector.
Text: none. No labels or markings anywhere.
Output: one complete high-resolution wide 16:9 landscape editorial image, full bleed. Original composition, not a screenshot or imitation of an existing campaign. No stock-corporate imagery, robot mascots, brand logos, watermark, fake metrics, dashboards, or mockup frame. Do not make a collage of multiple alternative designs.

title: Recording archive collage
sampleTitle: What your catalog archive can tell you
description: An illustrative collage built from a generated archive-style recording-studio image and invented paper fragments, with blue and lime accents. It suggests catalog exploration without depicting real historical source material.
composition: One large monochrome studio photo, a small paper fragment and restrained cutouts on warm ivory.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: editorial magazine collage.
Primary subject: one original monochrome archival-feeling photograph of a recording studio console and reel-to-reel equipment, with no people and no recognizable brand. This single photograph is the strong anchor, roughly two-thirds of the composition, not a contact sheet of many unrelated photos. Make the photograph feel like a found studio contact print with gentle silver-gelatin grain and real imperfect analog contrast, never a copied existing photograph.
Composition: warm ivory paper canvas, the anchoring black-and-white photograph placed slightly left of center at a tiny natural angle, close-cropped. Add only one small torn ivory paper fragment, a few slim abstract track-listing paper strips with nonlinguistic short dashes or blank bars (absolutely NO legible text or numbers), one bold matte Recoup-blue cutout partly overlapping a lower photo corner, and one very small lime registration accent. Editorial restraint and clear hierarchy; not a random moodboard. Paper overlaps and a few real soft edge shadows give tactility.
Palette: warm ivory #F8FAF5 dominant around the monochrome studio image, one bold blue #007EBD cut-paper area, one sparing lime #D6FF62 accent, forest-black #132B26 for dark tone.
Text: absolutely none. Any tiny equipment labeling is illegible, with no brand lettering. No title, letters, numbers, caption, logo or footer.
Output: one complete high-resolution wide 16:9 landscape editorial image, full bleed. Original composition, not a screenshot or imitation of an existing campaign. No stock-corporate imagery, robot mascots, brand logos, watermark, fake metrics, dashboards, or mockup frame. Do not make a collage of multiple alternative designs.

title: Sources through review
sampleTitle: How an AI workflow moves from source to review
description: A conceptual illustration of three grouped sources passing through one review checkpoint into an organized output. It explains a general review pattern; it is not a product screen or proof of an actual workflow.
composition: Three grouped shapes at left converge through a single central checkpoint into one organized shape at right.
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: original conceptual editorial illustration with no text.
Primary request: a clear routing illustration showing THREE grouped source shapes converging through ONE review checkpoint into ONE organized output. The idea should be readable purely through the composition, not labels.
Structure: on the left, three clearly separated small groups arranged vertically, each group made from two or three overlapping warm-ivory sheets or simple rounded shapes. Confident thin forest-green routing lines from those three groups converge into a single central review checkpoint: one larger ivory open circle with a small lime check mark inside. One forest line exits this checkpoint and leads to a single neatly aligned ivory output stack on the right. Small restrained arrowheads establish left-to-right flow. Each source group gets its own single clear path; all pass through the checkpoint, and only one path exits. No extra branches.
Style: mostly flat graphic illustration, assured printed lines with a tiny human irregularity, simple ivory shapes and almost no shading, generous spacing, strong visual hierarchy. A conceptual publication graphic, not miniature product UI or an app screenshot. Predominantly pale icy blue #C2EDFF backdrop, forest #132B26 lines, warm ivory #F8FAF5 shapes, one sparing lime #D6FF62 check. No blue gradient, glow or 3D rendering.
Text: none whatsoever. No labels, letters, numbers, axes, legends, metrics or analytics. No dashboards, interface chrome or mini windows.
Output: one complete high-resolution wide 16:9 landscape editorial image, full bleed. Original composition, not a screenshot or imitation of an existing campaign. No stock-corporate imagery, robot mascots, brand logos, watermark, fake metrics, dashboards, or mockup frame. Do not make a collage of multiple alternative designs.

title: Make AI useful
sampleTitle: Make AI useful in your music business
description: Large ivory type presents a direct editorial statement over vivid blue, with a restrained lime underline and fine-grain color glow.
composition: Three oversized left-aligned lines centered vertically, with a small lime underline and blue/lime glow below.
prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset type: bold editorial typographic cover, flat full-bleed printed artwork.
Input image role: use the supplied image ONLY as reference for vivid blue/lime color relationships and its fine flat grain, not its exact gradient geometry. Create a new composition.
Typography: exact words on THREE lines, rendered verbatim:
MAKE
AI
USEFUL.
Very large, sharp bold ivory #F8FAF5 grotesk sans-serif lettering, similar to DM Sans Bold, with clean familiar letterforms, confident weight and considered tight spacing. Left-aligned block placed centered-left and vertically centered; the lettering dominates the picture, occupies about two-thirds of its height, and is completely readable with all characters inside the image. Maintain the line breaks exactly: line one MAKE, line two AI, line three USEFUL. including the final period. Add just one small lime underline beneath the word USEFUL. No additional word.
Background: deep vivid blue #007EBD with #168DDD shifts, a fine-grain soft blue/lime #D6FF62 glow concentrated toward the bottom edge in a new asymmetric shape. Blue stays dominant. Smooth, flat, printed color with fine dry noise, no cellular or frosted-glass material. Strong type contrast.
Constraints: only the specified three text lines and lime underline. NO logo, footer, caption, extra text, explanatory labels, card, shadow on type, 3D letters, mockup surface or frame.
Output: one complete high-resolution wide 16:9 landscape editorial image, full bleed. Original composition, not a screenshot or imitation of an existing campaign. title: Blue passage and lime threshold
sampleTitle: Building systems your company can grow with
description: A quiet passage with blue plaster walls and a lime threshold uses real architectural space to suggest durable systems and room for growth.
composition: Strong diagonal view through a minimal passage, blue wall planes, ivory ceiling and narrow lime threshold.
prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: architectural editorial photograph.
Scene: a real-feeling minimalist architectural passage with matte sky-blue plaster walls, an ivory ceiling, and a narrow lime-painted threshold at a doorway further through the passage. No furniture, people or props. The passage should feel modest, physically built and inhabitable, not a futuristic monument or digital environment.
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 with a close, strong oblique diagonal perspective. One blue wall plane is cropped boldly in the foreground; the passage recedes through an offset doorway. The ivory ceiling cuts a crisp diagonal across the top. A narrow vivid lime threshold line makes a small deliberate interruption at the opening, integrated into the architecture rather than a glowing effect. Calm assured use of negative space, slightly asymmetrical, real lens perspective, natural architectural proportions.
Lighting: bright natural daylight entering from an opening outside the crop, making a dramatic clean-edged geometric shadow across one plaster plane. Retain detail in the shadows, realistic subtle plaster imperfections, daylight color and tactile matte paint. Editorial architectural photography, not 3D-render gloss.
Palette: sky-blue #168DDD and Recoup blue #007EBD wall planes, ivory #F8FAF5 ceiling and incidental floor, lime #D6FF62 narrow painted threshold. Let lighting produce real variations. No gradient backdrop.
Text: none. No signage, brand names, artwork, lettering or numbers.
Output: one complete high-resolution wide 16:9 landscape editorial image, full bleed. Original composition, not a screenshot or imitation of an existing campaign. No stock-corporate imagery, robot mascots, brand logos, watermark, fake metrics, dashboards, or mockup frame. Do not make a collage of multiple alternative designs.
